title: Transport of the pre-pushforward classical localization triangle
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Work with ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A$ on the small etale and pro-etale sites and their ordinary derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and $D^+$ for objects with cohomology vanishing sufficiently far below. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. For $B\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ put $D=i_{\mathrm{supp}}^	imes B$, using the ordinary etale closed-support right adjoint of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle], and assume $D\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Put $K=
u_X^*B$ and $L=
u_Z^*D$. Exact comparison inverse image and the canonical direct-image comparisons of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] identify the $
u_X^*$-image of the entire etale triangle
$$i_*D\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{\mathrm{et}}}B\xrightarrow{\eta_{j,\mathrm{et}}}Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}j_{\mathrm{et}}^*B\xrightarrow{b_{\mathrm{et}}}(i_*D)[1]$$
with a natural distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category]
$$i_*L\xrightarrow{\epsilon'}K\xrightarrow{\eta_j}Rj_*j^*K\xrightarrow{b'}(i_*L)[1].$$
The first arrow is the transported etale closed counit, the second arrow is the actual pro-etale open adjunction unit, and $b'$ is the transport of $b_{\mathrm{et}}$ with the canonical shift comparison. The identifications are natural in $B$, and use the canonical mate comparisons for $i$ and $j$, together with $j^*
u_X^*\cong
u_U^*j_{\mathrm{et}}^*$; in particular they specify the sign of the third arrow.

source.place: First localization triangle before Rp_*; finite direct-image transport (old item Step 3)

proof.text: Check the hypotheses for the direct-image comparisons. The coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ is finite and commutative by [def-pur-conventions]. The affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes $i$ quasi-compact: over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ its source is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$. Both $i$ and $j$ are monomorphisms, since they identify their source with a closed or open subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Their diagonals are therefore isomorphisms, hence quasi-compact, so they are quasi-separated. The quasi-compactness of $j$ is assumed. Thus both morphisms satisfy the quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypothesis of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison].

source.place: Direct-image comparison, hypothesis that g is quasi-compact and quasi-separated

proof.text: The etale closed direct image on constant-$A$ modules is exact, as stated in [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement]. Its pro-etale counterpart is exact by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact], whose quasi-compact-complement hypothesis is assumed here. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], their termwise functors are canonically their right derived functors; use these normalized identifications in every occurrence of the comparison for $i$. The comparison inverse images $F_T=\nu_T^*$ and the open inverse images are exact by [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], $F_X$ induces a triangulated functor with its termwise shift comparison $\sigma_M:F_X(M[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}F_X(M)[1]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], these exact inverse images preserve $D^+$, so $L=F_ZD$, $K=F_XB$, and $j_e^*B$ are bounded below. In particular the two inputs $D$ and $j_e^*B$ to the direct-image comparisons lie in their stated domains.

source.place: Tag 015F, label lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; proetale.tex Tag 09BM, label lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact

proof.text: Compare the two open direct images on the etale side. In [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle], $Rj_{e,*}$ is the total unbounded right derived functor with the unbounded adjunction $j_e^*\dashv Rj_{e,*}$. By contrast, [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] and [lem-pe-direct-image-mate-compatibility] use the bounded-below derived direct image $R^+j_{e,*}$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], together with its adjunction on $D^+$, whose unit is $\eta^+_e$. Every $M\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ is $QI$ for a bounded-below complex $I$ of injectives, and such an $I$ is K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative, prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. A K-injective complex computes the total derived functor [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], so $Rj_{e,*}M\cong Q(j_{e,*}I)$ is bounded below. Thus $Rj_{e,*}$ and, by Step 2, $j_e^*$ preserve $D^+$. The inclusion $D^+\subseteq D$ is full, so the unbounded adjunction restricts to an adjunction $j_e^*\dashv Rj_{e,*}|_{D^+}$ between the $D^+$ categories with the same unit $\eta_e$. Uniqueness of right adjoints gives a unique natural isomorphism $\mu:R^+j_{e,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_{e,*}|_{D^+}$ with $\mu_{j_e^*B}\circ\eta^+_{e,B}=\eta_{e,B}$ for every $B\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. On the pro-etale side, $Rj_{p,*}$ and its unit $\eta_p$ denote the bounded-below derived direct image and adjunction of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] and [lem-pe-direct-image-mate-compatibility]; $K$ and $j_p^*K$ are bounded below by Step 2.

source.place: Section 06XW (label section-unbounded): K-injective complexes compute RF; Lemma 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective); restriction of an adjunction to full subcategories and uniqueness of adjoints

proof.text:
Apply [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] to $B$ on the ordinary etale module derived category. Its right adjoint is precisely the $i_{\mathrm{supp}}^\times$ in the statement, so its first object is $i_{e,*}D$ and its first two arrows are $\epsilon_e$ and $\eta_e$. Write $Q_B=Rj_{e,*}j_e^*B$ and write $b_e:Q_B\to(i_{e,*}D)[1]$ for its third arrow. Applying the triangulated functor of [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] gives the distinguished triangle
$$F_X(i_{e,*}D)\xrightarrow{F_X\epsilon_e}K\xrightarrow{F_X\eta_e}F_XQ_B\xrightarrow{\sigma_{i_{e,*}D}\,F_X(b_e)}F_X(i_{e,*}D)[1].$$
This applies the functor to the given natural triangle, so its third arrow and naturality are retained.

source.place: Opening localization triangle, before applying Rp_*; etale source triangle is lem-exc-closed-support-triangle

proof.text:
Let $\beta_{g,M}:F_{\mathrm{target}(g)}Rg_{e,*}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_{p,*}F_{\mathrm{source}(g)}M$ be the canonical mate comparison of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]. Using the normalized exact-direct-image identifications of Step 2, put
$$\alpha_B=\beta_{i,D}:F_X(i_{e,*}D)\xrightarrow{\sim}i_{p,*}L.$$
Let $c_{j,B}:j_p^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}F_Uj_e^*B$ be the inverse-image comparison of that same theorem, and put
$$\gamma_B=Rj_{p,*}(c_{j,B}^{-1})\circ\beta_{j,j_e^*B}\circ F_X(\mu_{j_e^*B}^{-1}):F_XQ_B\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_{p,*}j_p^*K,$$
with $\mu$ the identification of Step 3.
All factors are natural isomorphisms. Step 1 verifies the geometric hypotheses for both $\beta$'s; Steps 2 and 3 verify their bounded-below input hypotheses. These are the canonical mate comparisons, with no independently chosen object isomorphism.

source.place: Inverse-image square and canonical derived mate, opening sentences; isomorphism for qcqs g

proof.text:
Use the explicit unit identity of [lem-pe-direct-image-mate-compatibility] with $g=j$ and its object $A$ there equal to $B$ here:
$$\beta_{j,j_e^*B}\circ F_X(\eta^+_{e,B})=Rj_{p,*}(c_{j,B})\circ\eta_{p,K}.$$
By Step 3, $F_X(\eta^+_{e,B})=F_X(\mu_{j_e^*B}^{-1})\circ F_X(\eta_{e,B})$. Composing with $Rj_{p,*}(c_{j,B}^{-1})$ therefore gives
$$\gamma_B\circ F_X(\eta_{e,B})=\eta_{p,K}.$$
Thus the second arrow after changing objects is the actual open adjunction unit. Define the first arrow by
$$\epsilon'_B=F_X(\epsilon_{e,B})\circ\alpha_B^{-1}:i_{p,*}L\to K.$$
Since $\epsilon_{e,B}$ is the closed-support counit by [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle], this is exactly the transported etale closed counit requested. No assertion about a right adjoint on arbitrary pro-etale inputs is needed.

source.place: Opening sentence: comparison adjoint to inverse-image square and etale counit, compatible with units and counits

proof.text:
Define the connecting arrow by the explicit formula
$$b'_B=\alpha_B[1]\circ\sigma_{i_{e,*}D}\circ F_X(b_{e,B})\circ\gamma_B^{-1}.$$
Then $(\alpha_B,1_K,\gamma_B)$ is an isomorphism from the triangle of Step 4 to
$$i_{p,*}L\xrightarrow{\epsilon'_B}K\xrightarrow{\eta_{p,K}}Rj_{p,*}j_p^*K\xrightarrow{b'_B}(i_{p,*}L)[1].$$
For the first square use $\epsilon'_B\alpha_B=F_X\epsilon_e$; the second square is Step 6; the last square is $b'_B\gamma_B=\alpha_B[1]\sigma_{i_{e,*}D}F_Xb_e$, by the displayed definition. Isomorphism invariance of distinguished triangles (TR1 in [def-weil-triangulated-category]) proves distinguishedness. This formula uses the given shift comparison and adds no rotation or negative sign, so it specifies the sign of the entire transported third arrow.

source.place: Tag 0145, label definition-triangulated-category: TR1, invariance under triangle isomorphisms

proof.text:
Finally let $h:B\to\widetilde B$ be a morphism of bounded-below inputs for which both support objects are bounded below, and put $d=i_{\mathrm{supp}}^\times(h)$. The natural etale triangle of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] has components $(i_{e,*}d,h,Rj_{e,*}j_e^*h)$, including its last square. Apply $F_X$ and conjugate this triangle morphism by $(\alpha,1,\gamma)$ for its source and target. Naturality of the comparisons in [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] gives components $(i_{p,*}F_Zd,F_Xh,Rj_{p,*}j_p^*F_Xh)$. The last square reads
$$(i_{p,*}F_Zd)[1]\circ b'_B=b'_{\widetilde B}\circ Rj_{p,*}j_p^*(F_Xh).$$
It follows directly by substituting Step 7's formula, using the last square of the etale triangle, and then naturality of $\alpha,\gamma,\sigma$ (for $\gamma$ including that of $\mu$ from Step 3). This proves naturality of every arrow, including the signed connecting arrow.
